posts.cooked: To change the stubject a bit, but keeping it around the same hero...One thing that's come up with Chrono Ranger is with his Ultimate Target bounty, which lets Jim use a power the first time that target deals damage each turn. I think this is one of those "deas damage versus dealt damage" issues again but...if the target deals damage but that damage is soaked (eg the target with Ultimate Target on it tries to hit Legacy for one point of damage but he has Fortitude out and so takes no damage), does Chrono Ranger still get to use a power? It doesn't specify that hp has to be reduced for him to do so, but I seem to recall there are other cases where someone who's dealt no damage (eg Ra when he has Flame Barrier up) doesn't get to trigger an effect. Then again, those tend to specify that the target's hp has to be reduced for their effect to go off. I'm guessing that whatever the case regarding Ultimate Target damage, it'd be the same if the target of the attack was immune to damage as well, since the bountied target is still trying to deal them damage - it's just that nothing is happening.

posts.name: jagarciao
posts.cooked:
Ha, now we are entering the existentialist debate on what it means to be or not be a card and what entering play and leaving play means. 

As mentioned by many others, I can see your point in saying that nothing has "left play" but that the target aspect of that card has simply "ceased to be" or something of that manner... but until we get an official ruling that in game terms these to things are defined differently, I believe that the logical conclusion that if something was in play, but is no longer there then it must have "left play" or somehow been "removed from play" because we have no other game terminology to explain this phenomenon. We have a lot of other words and phrases to describe such actions in the English language, but within the definitions of the game we do not.

posts.name: Ronway
posts.cooked:
Have no fear folks! I have gotten the answer we all have been waiting for in this crazy topic for oh so long. If you don't want to click the attachment, then i'll type it. 

 

When a Target suddenly becomes not a Target anymore, such as when The Operative flips, that Target has left play. When something that was not a Target suddenly becomes a Target, such as when Miss Informatio​n flips, that Target has entered play.
